source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify primary official reporting sources for COVID-19 human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in New York (state and city) during 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NYSDOH and NYC DOHMH are the authoritative subnational agencies publishing weekly COVID-19 surveillance data for New York. Their dashboards, weekly reports, and data downloads are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC state-level COVID-19 surveillance data covering New York for the week of 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC publishes state-level COVID-19 case, death, and hospitalization data through its COVID Data Tracker and associated datasets, which may include New York-specific breakdowns for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HHS Protect or HealthData.gov structured datasets reporting New York COVID-19 hospitalizations for the target week.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: HHS Protect publishes hospital-level and state-level COVID-19 hospitalization data as open structured datasets, which may contain New York records for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent summary or structured sources (e.g., WHO situation reports, PAHO, Our World in Data) to compare against collected New York COVID-19 records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Held-back or independent aggregator sources support masked validation of case and death counts without contaminating the primary collection pipeline.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured open-data portals (e.g., NYC Open Data, New York State Open Data) with COVID-19 datasets covering the target window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Open data portals may publish machine-readable COVID-19 datasets that can serve as independent validation against official agency narrative reports.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify context sources clarifying COVID-19 case definitions, count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), and reporting period conventions used by New York agencies in early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definition and count-type context is essential for correct normalization of extracted records, especially given the transition in COVID-19 reporting frameworks in 2023–2024.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints reporting New York COVID-19 epidemiology for January 2024 or the surrounding period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources may provide case definitions, variant context (JN.1 wave), and epidemiological framing useful for interpreting extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports covering New York COVID-19 case and death trends during the first week of January 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may surface early outbreak signals, reference official figures, or link to official dashboards not yet identified through direct agency searches.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources with ambiguous geographic scope (e.g., national aggregates without NY breakdown), unclear count semantics, or validation leakage risk for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources that cannot be clearly assigned to collection or validation, or whose counts cannot be unambiguously attributed to the target window and location, must be flagged before entering extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: NYSDOH, NYC DOHMH, and CDC are the primary authoritative agencies publishing COVID-19 case, death, and hospitalization surveillance data for New York. NYSDOH publishes weekly COVID-19 reports; NYC DOHMH publishes city-level data; CDC COVID Data Tracker publishes state-level breakdowns. These are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 window.

Structured open-data portals such as NYC Open Data, New York State Open Data, HealthData.gov, and HHS Protect publish machine-readable COVID-19 datasets that can serve as independent validation sources. These datasets may include daily or weekly case, death, and hospitalization counts for New York.
WHO situation reports and PAHO regional updates may include US or New York COVID-19 data for the target window, providing an independent validation layer against official agency figures.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints covering New York COVID-19 epidemiology in early 2024 (e.g., JN.1 variant wave) provide case definitions, count semantics, and epidemiological context for interpreting extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., New York Times, AP, local NY outlets) and situation reports may cite official New York COVID-19 figures for the first week of January 2024, providing collection support and pointers to official sources.

source_planning_risks.risk: A source intended for validation may leak into collection if roles are not enforced during later discovery.
source_planning_risks.mitigation: Keep validation-reserved sources separate until evaluation.

source_planning_risks.risk: Cumulative, annual, newly reported, and suspected counts may be mixed across source categories.
source_planning_risks.mitigation: Require evidence quotes and count-semantics fields.
